title: ConstraintUnit
description: The minimal, indivisible unit of a SemanticAnchor constraint. A ConstraintUnit anchors a NAMED ENTITY REFERENCE — anything the model must not hallucinate: a field, parameter, enum, or symbol (function/method/module name) — to a verifiable contract. Atomic units are scalar references; composite entities (signatures, endpoints) are compositions of units via `members`. It constrains the REFERENCE (existence / name / shape / values / policy), never the LOGIC. Intentionally domain-agnostic: the financial field registry it was extracted from is one population of ConstraintUnits. See docs/design.md.

id.description: Canonical identifier the model should converge on. snake_case, stable.

kind.description: What kind of named reference this unit anchors. 'field'/'param'/'enum'/'symbol' are atomic; 'signature'/'endpoint' are composite (see `members`). Orthogonal to `type` (which is the data type).

description.description: What this entity means, in plain language.

aliases.description: Natural-language or system-specific names that should resolve to this id. This is the 'best-effort' surface: resolve() matches against these, but a miss is normal in open-world tasks and must NOT be treated as an error.

type.description: Primitive data type of the entity.

provenance.description: WHERE this constraint came from. This is the core open-world extension over a static registry. 'declared' = pre-curated, stable, closed-world (the field-registry case). 'derived' = computed from the runtime environment (AST, type system, lint config, tests). 'emergent' = accumulated during a session (e.g. a user said 'keep backward compatibility' mid-task).

source.description: Concrete origin for traceability. For declared: a registry name. For derived: 'typescript', 'eslint', 'pytest', etc. For emergent: 'session:<turn>'.

constraints.description: Domain-agnostic shape constraints — the verifiable contract. Abstracted from field-registry's `inherentRules`. NEGATIVE LIST (do NOT put here): business thresholds, cross-entity rules, time-varying policy. Those belong to a rule engine, not to a ConstraintUnit.

required.description: Whether the entity must be present.

min.description: Numeric lower bound (intrinsic to the type, not a business threshold).

max.description: Numeric upper bound (intrinsic to the type, not a business threshold).

checksum.description: Standard checksum algorithm (e.g. luhn for card numbers).

format.description: Standard format shorthand; verifiers derive a concrete check from it.

values.description: Enumerated legal values (when type=enum). Abstracted from field-registry's enum service.

policies.description: Generic, non-business policy tags that a harness can act on. Domain-agnostic: 'sensitive'/'pii' replace the registry's financial maskRule values. The harness decides what each policy enforces (e.g. masking, no-logging, immutability).

mappings.description: Cross-context name mappings — how this entity is named in other systems/contexts. Abstracted from field-registry's `systems`, with all financial DB specifics removed.

name.description: The name used in that context.

members.description: Composition for COMPOSITE entities (kind=signature/endpoint). Each member references another ConstraintUnit by id and gives its structural role. This is how a signature stays honest: it is a bag of atomic units + structure (order/role), not a magic single unit. Omit for atomic units.

role.description: Structural role of this member within the composite.
